patch.value: A promoted generation could store a padded or blank approval identity, consuming none of the budget it was promoted under

The approved promotion budget is counted by comparing each promoted generation's stored approval to the approval item id with strict equality. The parse boundary trimmed parent but not approval, and accepted an empty approval because it is non-null and so satisfies the promotion-evidence invariant. A generation body carrying an approval of two spaces, or of the approval id with surrounding whitespace, was therefore promoted while matching no approval id and consuming none of that approval's budget.

value.text: Reported by CodeRabbit on unbraind/pm-rl#12 as a Major data-integrity finding, and reproduced before it was applied: parseGenerationSpec trimmed parent at the parse boundary but stored approval verbatim, while countPromotedUnderApproval compares the stored approval to the approval id by strict equality. A hand-authored Generation body is all that is needed; the promote command never has to be called with a padded flag.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fixed at the parse boundary rather than at the comparison, and a blank approval is refused as empty_approval rather than normalized to null. Normalizing a blank to null would silently downgrade a promoted record to one missing its evidence, so the promotion-evidence invariant would then report a different defect than the one present. The promote command also trims its approval flag so the id it looks up and the identity it stores are the same string.

value.note: Parse boundary normalization holds at the 100/100/100 coverage gate

value.text: An identity that is compared by strict equality must be normalized where it is parsed, not where it is compared, and every such field must be normalized together. This defect existed only because a previous round trimmed parent and stopped there: the same file, the same parse function, the same failure mode, one field later. When a normalization bug is fixed, enumerate every stored identity in the record and fix the class.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: A blank value that is non-null passes any invariant written as a null check. The promotion-evidence invariant asks whether approval is non-null, so an empty string satisfied it while matching no approval id - the record was simultaneously promoted-with-evidence and promoted-under-nothing. Presence checks on identity fields must test for a usable identity, not for the absence of null.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round seven produced five findings. Four were applied. One was refused with evidence: the claim that a padded --parent reaches storage is false, because stringOption returns value.trim() and maps a blank to undefined, so the value is already normalized before the register command sees it. The proposed fix would have restated a normalization the boundary already performs. Kept as an end-to-end guard on the option boundary instead, verified by removing the trim from stringOption and confirming the test fails.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: The same evidence corrects something I asserted in the previous round and CodeRabbit stored as a learning: I said trimming --approval was needed because normalizing only the parse side would leave --approval with surrounding whitespace failing a lookup it should satisfy. That was wrong. stringOption had already trimmed it, so the flag-side trim was redundant from the start and has been removed. The parse-boundary normalization is the one that matters, because a generation body can be hand-authored without ever passing through the flag.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: An absent parent key was refused as invalid_parent with a message stating parent must be a string or null - for a seed body whose absent parent IS null. Every other optional field in the parser already collapsed undefined to null before validating; parent was the last that did not. Fixed, with the non-seed case still refused but now for the reason true of it (missing_parent) rather than for a type it never violated.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Both refusals were withdrawn by the reviewer with explicit reasoning. On the parent trim it accepted that stringOption normalizes before the command sees the value, and accepted the correction that the same applies to approvalId - stating that the meaningful normalization is in parseGenerationSpec because persisted specifications bypass command-option processing. On the history edit it accepted that comment_edit is an appended hash-bound correction event that does not rewrite the earlier comment_add, and said it had applied an existing pm-history learning too broadly. Recording this because a refusal that is accepted is only worth the evidence attached to it: both were reproduced or read off the actual file before being argued.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: The fastest way to test a review finding is to write the test it implies and watch what happens. A finding that is true produces a failing test; a finding that is false produces a passing one, which is indistinguishable from a vacuous test unless you already know which you are looking at. Both cases here were resolved that way in minutes, and one of them exposed an error in my own previous round that had already been stored as a reviewer learning.
